title.value: Technology-enhanced trauma training in low-resource settings: A scoping review and feasibility analysis of educational technologies
title.justification: The paper's title, 'Technology-enhanced trauma training in low-resource settings: A scoping review and feasibility analysis of educational technologies,' clearly describes its focus on trauma training technologies suitable for low-resource settings.
title.quote: Technology-enhanced trauma training in low-resource settings: A scoping review and feasibility analysis of educational technologies

extractions.description: This paper reviews current educational technologies used in trauma training and evaluates their feasibility for low- and lower-middle-income countries (LMICs). Through a scoping review, the study assesses technologies like high-fidelity mannequins, virtual simulation, and digital courses, especially considering their suitability for LMIC contexts. The paper aims to identify the best training technologies that can optimize learning outcomes in trauma courses and are feasible for low-resource settings.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is enhancing trauma training in low-resource settings using educational technologies, which indirectly contributes to sustainability by improving medical capacity but doesn't directly address climate or ecological sustainability themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Background: Lack of training contributes to the burden of trauma-related mortality and morbidity in low- and lower-middle-income countries (LMICs). Educational technologies present a unique opportu-nity to enhance the quality of trauma training.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly address Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development themes. Its focus is on improving medical training technologies for better healthcare outcomes in LMICs.
primary_category.quote: Given the urgent need for pediatric trauma training, educators must use technologies that optimize learning outcomes and remain feasible for low-resource settings.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper addresses challenges specific to low- and lower-middle-income countries, which are often part of the Global South. It discusses educational technologies that are feasible in these low-resource settings.
secondary_categories.quote: The burden is disproportionately greater in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where 90% of injury-related deaths occur.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fit any sub-category related to Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development, as it primarily addresses trauma training technology feasibility.
primary_sub_category.quote: To our knowledge, this is the first study to perform a feasibility analysis of trauma training technologies in the LMIC context.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper indirectly supports policy advice and knowledge sharing by identifying feasible educational technologies for trauma training in low-resource settings, which could inform policy decisions in LMICs.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We identified that the majority of trauma courses in the literature use technologies which are less suitable for LMICs.

new_primary_category.justification: The scope of the paper is not aligned with any Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development categories, focusing instead on medical training technologies.
new_primary_category.quote: Educational technologies present a unique opportunity to enhance the quality of trauma training.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category applicable to Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development can be created from this paper's focus on trauma training technologies.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We conducted a scoping review evaluating the learning outcomes of technology-enhanced training in general trauma assessment.
